title: Sum of Tate residues above a closed point under field extension
statement:
Let $k$ be any field and $C/k$ a smooth projective geometrically connected curve [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $K/k$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension], let $p:C_K=C\times_k K\to C$ be the projection [def-pc-base-change], and let $x$ be a closed point of $C$. Write $F=k(C)$ and $F_K=K(C_K)$ for the function fields, and $\eta\in\Omega^1_{F/k}$ for a rational differential [def-sc-function-field, def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $\eta_K\in\Omega^1_{F_K/K}$ be its image under the map induced by $F\to F_K$ and $k\to K$. Use the $k$-valued and $K$-valued Tate residues of [sk-thm-picard-duality], defined by the finite-potent trace construction, without imposing separability on $\kappa(x)/k$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Then
$$\sum_{y\in |\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(x)\otimes_k K)|}\operatorname{res}_{y,C_K/K}(\eta_K)=\iota\bigl(\operatorname{res}_{x,C/k}(\eta)\bigr),$$
where $\iota:k\to K$ is the field inclusion and the finite sum runs over the underlying closed points of the fibre $p^{-1}(x)$; a nonreduced fibre is not replaced by a separable fibre, and no extra multiplicity is inserted into this sum.

source.place: pp. 149–155: §1 finite-potent traces; §2 Theorem 1 and finite-terms formula (*) on p. 152, (R1), (R5); §3 local residues. Scalar-extension consequence of this construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-curve-local-scalar-principal-parts]. Write $L=F_K$, $O=\mathcal O_{C,x}$, $S=\{y\mid x\}$, $A=O\otimes_kK$, $V=F\otimes_kK$ and $B=\bigcap_{y\in S}O_y$, all inside $L$. Fix a uniformizer $t$ of $O$. This gives $V=A[t^{-1}]$, $L=B[t^{-1}]$, $V\cap B=A$, the two principal-parts isomorphisms, and finite-dimensional quotients by $t^n$. In particular $S$ is finite, including when the fibre algebra is nonreduced. We first compute on $f\,dg$ for $f,g\in F$.

source.place: §3 local lattices, pp. 154–155; agent scalar-extension argument using semilocal principal parts.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus] to the $k$-algebra $F$, the $F$-module $F$ and the subspace $O$, and to the $K$-algebra $V$, the $V$-module $V$ and the subspace $A$. By [lem-pc-tate-dvr-residue-calculus], $(fO+O)/O$ is finite-dimensional for $f\in F$, so $O$ is admissible, and for a $k$-linear projection $\pi:F\to O$ fixing $O$ and $f,g\in F$ the operator $T=[\pi m_f,m_g]$ is finite-potent with $\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm fp}(T)=\operatorname{res}_{x,C/k}(f\,dg)$. Here $A$ is admissible for $V$ over $K$: every element of $V$ is a finite sum $\sum c_i(f_i\otimes1)$ with $c_i\in K$, each $f_iO$ lies in some $t^{-n_i}O$, so one common $n$ gives $rA\subset t^{-n}A$, and $t^{-n}A/A\simeq A/t^nA$ is finite-dimensional by step 1. The map $\pi\otimes1:V\to A$ is a $K$-linear projection fixing $A$, and $m_{f\otimes1}=m_f\otimes1$, $m_{g\otimes1}=m_g\otimes1$ on $V=F\otimes_kK$, so $[(\pi\otimes1)m_{f\otimes1},m_{g\otimes1}]=T\otimes1$. Choose $N$ and a finite-dimensional $T$-stable $U\subset F$ containing $T^N(F)$. Then $(T\otimes1)^N(V)=T^N(F)\otimes_kK\subset U\otimes_kK$, which is $T\otimes1$-stable and finite-dimensional over $K$; in the basis $u_i\otimes1$ coming from a $k$-basis $u_i$ of $U$, the matrix of $T\otimes1$ is $\iota$ applied to the matrix of $T|_U$, so its trace is $\iota(\operatorname{Tr}(T|_U))$. By the projection formula of [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus],
$$\operatorname{res}_{V,A}((f\otimes1)\,d(g\otimes1))=\iota(\operatorname{res}_{x,C/k}(f\,dg)).$$

source.place: §1 (T1) and definition of the finite-potent trace, p. 150; §2 Theorem 1, p. 151; scalar extension is the explicit matrix calculation.

proof.text: For each $r\in R=V\subset L$, some $t^n r$ belongs to $B$ since $L=B[t^{-1}]$. Hence $rB\subset t^{-n}B$, and $t^{-n}B/B\simeq B/t^nB$ is finite-dimensional by [lem-pc-curve-local-scalar-principal-parts]. Thus $B$ is admissible as a $K$-subspace of the $R$-module $L$. Apply [lem-pc-tate-residue-exact-sequence] to $0\to V\to L\to L/V\to0$ with lattice $B$. Its inverse-image lattice is $A$ by $V\cap B=A$. Its image lattice is all of $L/V$: for any $l\in L$, surjectivity of $V/A\to L/B$ provides $v\in V$ with $l-v\in B$. The residue for the full lattice on $L/V$ is zero by [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus], since that lattice is an $R$-submodule. Therefore $\operatorname{res}_{L,B}=\operatorname{res}_{V,A}$ on $\Omega^1_{R/K}$.

source.place: §1 (T2), §2 Theorem 1: exact-sequence comparison with full quotient lattice; agent argument.

proof.text: Let $W=\prod_{y\in S}L$, $P=\prod_{y\in S}O_y$ and $j:L\to W$ the diagonal map. Regard these as $R=V$-modules. Each $O_y$ is admissible: a common power $t^n$ clears the denominator of $r\in R$ in $O_y$, and $O_y/t^nO_y$ is finite-dimensional by [lem-pc-curve-local-scalar-principal-parts]. The same bound and the finite product give admissibility of $P$. Apply [lem-pc-tate-residue-exact-sequence] to $0\to L\xrightarrow{j}W\to W/j(L)\to0$. The inverse-image lattice is $B$. The image lattice is the full quotient: given $(l_y)$, the surjection $L/B\to\bigoplus_y L/O_y$ gives $l\in L$ such that $l_y-l\in O_y$ for all $y$. The full lattice $W/j(L)$ is an $R$-submodule, so its residue is zero by [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus]. We obtain $\operatorname{res}_{W,P}=\operatorname{res}_{L,B}$.

source.place: §1 (T2), §2 and §3 finite sum of local residues, pp. 155–156; diagonal exact-sequence argument.

proof.text:
Choose a $K$-linear projection $\pi_y:L\to O_y$ in every coordinate and take their product. For $f,g\in F$, the commutator on $W$ is block diagonal with blocks $[\pi_y m_f,m_g]$. By [lem-pc-tate-dvr-residue-calculus] (for the DVR $O_y$ over $K$ with fraction field $L$) each block is finite-potent with trace $\operatorname{res}_{y,C_K/K}(f_K\,dg_K)$, and by [lem-pc-tate-abstract-residue-calculus] $\operatorname{res}_{W,P}((f\otimes1)d(g\otimes1))$ is the finite-potent trace of the block-diagonal operator for the product projection. Choose a common exponent $N$ and finite-dimensional stable subspaces containing their $N$th images. Their finite product is stable and contains the $N$th image of the block diagonal operator; a concatenation of bases shows its ordinary trace is the sum of the block traces. Thus
$$\operatorname{res}_{W,P}((f\otimes1)d(g\otimes1))=\sum_{y\in S}\operatorname{res}_{y,C_K/K}(f_K\,dg_K).$$
Combining this with steps 2–4 proves the required identity for $f\,dg$. This uses the same action of $f,g$ whether it is viewed through $R\to L$ or directly through $L$: the displayed multiplication operators on each coordinate are identical.

source.place: §1 definition of finite-potent trace and §3 finite-product calculation in Theorem 3, pp. 155–156.

proof.text: By the definition of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], every $\eta\in\Omega^1_{F/k}$ is a finite sum $\sum_i f_i\,dg_i$. The induced differential map takes this sum to $\sum_i f_{i,K}\,dg_{i,K}$. The local Tate residue maps are linear by [lem-pc-tate-dvr-residue-calculus]. Add the identities of step 5 and interchange the two finite sums. This gives the asserted formula for $\eta$. Each block in step 5 occurs once for a point of $S$; the trace uses the full quotients $O_y/t^nO_y$, so nilpotent thickness is already present in the operator, without an additional multiplicity on the sum.

source.place: §2 Theorem 1, linearity of residues; agent assembly of the scalar-extension identity.

proof_origin.place: §2 formula (*) p. 152 and §3 finite-product residues; explicit scalar-extension and semilocal exact-sequence argument.
